clue.text: It sounds like awareness signified motivation

indicators.note: It sounds like tells the solver to say the following phrase out loud and write what is heard

parts.note: awareness is insight, and signified means meant: together they are spoken as one phrase

explanation.surface: A remark about how being aware of something signals a person's drive or purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirring someone up to act is giving them a motive, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: A bit of a character in Greece

definitions.meaning: a tiny amount, the smallest scrap
a letter of the Greek alphabet, the one equivalent to i

explanation.surface: A small part of someone with personality who lives in Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth Greek letter is the smallest one, so its name also means a minute quantity.

clue.text: Firm gets million quid making chemicals

parts.note: CO, short for company, a business firm
quid is British slang for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A company earns a million pounds by manufacturing chemicals.
explanation.walkthrough: Quid is everyday British slang for a pound in money; the plural is taken here as POUNDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Substances made of two or more elements bonded together are chemicals, a plural noun for plural noun.

clue.text: Bound, around end of supper, to be ready for bed?

indicators.note: around says the word for bound wraps round the next letter

parts.note: bound in the sense of fastened with rope gives tied

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word supper

explanation.surface: Someone tied up after the last of supper, ready to go to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Being weary enough to want sleep is being ready for bed, the question mark flagging the loose fit.

clue.text: Without hesitation, miser surprisingly becomes more homely

indicators.note: Without in its old sense of outside: the shuffled letters go round the hesitation
surprisingly signals that the letters of miser come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: UM is the sound of hesitating in speech

explanation.surface: A miser who stops hesitating oddly turns more cosy and domestic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside here, not lacking: MSIER (miser rearranged after 'surprisingly') goes round UM.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumsy describes something cosy and homely like a mother's style, so the comparative fits more homely.

clue.text: Heads offering some children odd lessons

indicators.note: offering some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Head teachers providing a few unusual lessons for pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: Noddle is informal slang for a person's head, so the plural matches heads.

clue.text: Support something put on stage

definitions.meaning: a post or beam that holds something up
an object used by actors in a theatre production

explanation.surface: Backing a theatre production's scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a structural strut and, shortened from property, a piece of theatre equipment.

clue.text: Predominance needs control — little good in it

indicators.note: in it says the short letter goes inside the word for control

parts.note: a rein is a strap used to control a horse, hence to rein in
G is the short form of good

explanation.surface: To dominate you must keep control while being only a little bit good.
explanation.definitionFit: A period of rule or prevailing influence is dominance, so a monarch's rule is predominance.

clue.text: Following appeals, there's a new attempt to bring jocularity

indicators.note: Following tells us the remaining pieces come after the word for appeals

parts.note: pleas are earnest appeals or requests
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: After pleading fails, someone tries a fresh approach with humour.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, joking remark is a piece of jocularity, a good-humoured bit of banter.

clue.text: Maybe watch and relax, lying back

indicators.note: lying back says the word for relax is written backwards

parts.note: to remit is to relax or ease off, as with a penalty

explanation.surface: Perhaps have a look and unwind, lounging back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a verb with 'relax'; it is a noun, a timepiece, with 'Maybe' marking it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A wristwatch is one kind of timekeeping device, hence the hedge in the definition.

clue.text: Domineers, being out to introduce new ideas

indicators.note: being out suggests the letters of domineers are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Bossy types are ousted so that fresh thinking can come in.
explanation.definitionFit: To update something is to bring in new ideas and methods, both verbs.

clue.text: Enlists awkward person, the first person to be nabbed

indicators.note: to be nabbed says the pronoun is caught inside the shuffled letters
awkward signals the letters of person come out in a clumsy new order

parts.note: I is the first person singular pronoun

explanation.surface: A recruiter signs up a difficult person, the first to be arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be nabbed' puts I inside ROPESN, the letters of person rearranged by 'awkward'.
explanation.definitionFit: To persuade someone to join in is to enlist them, an idiom for drafting help.

clue.text: Father William maybe as personification of law enforcement

parts.note: the old man is slang for one's father, giving old
Bill is the usual short form of the name William

explanation.surface: Father William, perhaps, standing as an emblem of the police.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Bill is British slang for the police as a body.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang name treats the whole police force as one figure, personifying the law.

clue.text: Irish money once used in bets

definitions.meaning: the currency of Ireland before the euro, the Irish pound
wagers, as in having a flutter

explanation.surface: Old Irish currency being staked in wagers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish pound was called the punt, and a punt is also informal British English for a bet.

clue.text: Outlaws supporting teachers of traditional law

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting
the scribes of the Bible taught and interpreted Jewish law

explanation.surface: Bandits backing the scholars of ancient law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaws' looks like a plural noun for bandits but is a verb: bans.
explanation.definitionFit: To ban or forbid something officially is to outlaw it, both verbs in the present tense.

clue.text: Tenant, one bound to become investor

indicators.note: bound means enclosing, so the word for tenant encloses one

parts.note: a renter is someone who pays rent, a tenant
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tenant who is destined to become an investor in property.
explanation.definitionFit: A person living on income from property or investments is the French-derived term for an investor.

clue.text: Inclination to inactivity during time — time I kept in

parts.note: in means during, as in in the morning

indicators.note: kept in says the short pieces are held inside the word for an age

parts.note: an era is a period of time
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A tendency to idleness over a period, with time spent indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Sluggishness, a tendency to stay at rest and resist change, is a lean towards inactivity.

clue.text: Sitting among possessions

indicators.note: among says the answer is found inside the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Seated in the middle of one's belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sitting' looks like a verb; it is a noun, a meeting of a court or parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting of a court or council is a sitting, a period of formal business.

clue.text: Awfully nice saint — saint losing heart or keeping going?

indicators.note: awfully signals the letters of nice are badly arranged
losing heart says the middle letter of the second saint is removed

explanation.surface: A very kind saint, or one who has lost courage but carries on?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' gives INCE from nice; 'losing heart' drops the middle I of saint, leaving SANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unceasing carries on without stopping, so it is keeping going.

clue.text: Delay when American gets locked in shed

indicators.note: gets locked in says the abbreviation is shut inside the word for shed

parts.note: to shed money is to spend or lay it out

explanation.surface: A hold-up when a US citizen is shut inside a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a garden hut but is a verb meaning to give out.
explanation.definitionFit: To put off or postpone something is to delay it, both verbs.

clue.text: Cavorting man torn asunder

indicators.note: torn suggests the letters of asunder are ripped apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A capering man is ripped into pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The French term for a male ballet dancer names a man who leaps and twirls on stage.

clue.text: Soldiers taking exceptional care — someone posing a threat

parts.note: men are soldiers, the ranks as opposed to officers

indicators.note: exceptional suggests the letters of care are in an unusual arrangement

explanation.surface: Troops treating something with special caution because someone is threatening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptional' looks like praise for the care but signals the anagram, ACER.
explanation.definitionFit: One who menaces or intimidates others is a person issuing threats.

clue.text: Grew up and got married outside biblical city

indicators.note: outside says the word for wed goes round the city

parts.note: mated means paired off or wed
Ur of the Chaldees is the city of Abraham in the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone came of age and wed beyond the walls of an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming fully adult or ripe is growing up, both in the past tense.

clue.text: Grub when son's got in bed

indicators.note: got in says the letter for son is put inside the word for grub

parts.note: to grub is to dig or rummage, to root about
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Food for when the boy has climbed into bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like food but is a verb, to dig about.
explanation.definitionFit: A perch where birds settle for the night is their bed, and the word is used jokingly of people's beds.

clue.text: Be found as old dog going round about

indicators.note: going round says the word for dog surrounds the short letter

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Turning up as an elderly dog circles around.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist or be present somewhere is to be found there, as in a species found in Asia.

clue.text: Marks — no marks of approval when a letter is misprinted!

indicators.note: when a letter is misprinted says one letter of the phrase is swapped for another

parts.note: ticks are the marks a teacher puts against correct answers

explanation.surface: A teacher's grading, with no ticks because of a typing error.
explanation.walkthrough: NO TICKS has its K changed to E.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice something is to mark or observe it, both verbs in the third person.

clue.text: Feature of mountain with ice, no end a pain

parts.note: a col is a pass or saddle between mountain peaks

indicators.note: no end says the final letter of ice is dropped

parts.note: ice taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A mountain's icy features causing endless suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe abdominal pain, especially in babies, is a kind of pain.

clue.text: Hard look that may spread over man's face

definitions.text: that may spread over man's face

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
an air is a look or appearance, as in an air of confidence

explanation.surface: A stern glance that might pass across a man's expression.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an expression spreading over a face; read literally it is a beard growing there.
explanation.definitionFit: A beard or moustache is growth that spreads over a man's face.

clue.text: Retreating youngster can always become an adventurer

indicators.note: Retreating says the word for youngster runs backwards

parts.note: a cub is a young animal or a junior scout
can taken as written
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A child backing away can always turn into a daring explorer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate or buccaneer is an adventurer, someone seeking fortune by daring and risk.

clue.text: Animal Buddhist monk found by lake

indicators.note: found by says the two pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk or teacher

explanation.surface: A creature that a Tibetan monk came across beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American camelid is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Old worker engaged by wiser folk

indicators.note: engaged by says the answer is held within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: An elderly labourer hired by more sensible people.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal labourer bound to the land is a worker of medieval times.

clue.text: A creator? I'd set out to be different!

definitions.text: A creator? I'd set out to be different!

indicators.note: set out suggests the letters are laid out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone protesting that, far from being a maker, they aim to be quite unlike one.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of A CREATOR plus ID, rearranged, give someone who is the opposite of a creator.
explanation.definitionFit: One who wipes things out destroys rather than makes, the very contrary of a creator.
